title: Council protocol envelopes
description: One request/reply/event family used on both hops: page to wrapper, and wrapper to backend. Mutating requests carry base_revision (checked against the snapshot) and request_id (the idempotency key), so a retried command can never apply twice and a command written against a stale view is refused rather than merged.

Command.description: snapshot.get and source.fetch and definition.export are reads: they omit base_revision and never advance the snapshot. Everything else mutates.

base_revision.description: Required on a mutating command. Must equal the current snapshot_revision or the reply is a stale_revision error carrying the current snapshot.

Reply.description: Every reply carries the snapshot_revision it was produced against, so a view that applies replies out of order can detect it and re-read rather than render a mixture.

replayed.description: True when this request_id was already applied and the stored reply is being returned unchanged.

Event.description: One-way push towards the view. An event never carries authority: it announces that something moved, and the view re-reads what it needs. Most events originate in the backend; the two council.*_changed events about the surface itself originate in the native wrapper, which is the only participant that can see the host's theme and focus.

event.description: council.theme_changed carries {dark, background, text, font_size} read off the panel's own inherited theme; council.focus_changed carries {focused}. Both are the wrapper's, not the engine's, and neither says anything about the record.

Ready.description: The page announcing that its injected bridge exists. It is the only envelope that travels page-to-wrapper without being a request, and it exists because an eval() into a document that has no window.council yet is silently lost: until this arrives the wrapper queues everything it would push. A page reload announces again and is re-primed. It never reaches the backend.
